name: 51 (card game)
description: 51 is a point-collection card game played in China and Japan. Players collect cards of the same suit; A-K-Q-J-10 of one suit scores 51 points. Chinese version: draw, discard, exchange; first to 500+ wins. Japanese version: pick board cards, discard; call "Stop!" with best hand; highest single-suit total wins.

overview.description: 51 is a point-collection card game played in China and Japan. Players collect cards of the same suit; A-K-Q-J-10 of one suit scores 51 points. Chinese version: draw, discard, exchange; first to 500+ wins. Japanese version: pick board cards, discard; call "Stop!" with best hand; highest single-suit total wins.

history.origins: Point-collection game; Chinese and Japanese variants. A-K-Q-J-10 in one suit = 51 points. Chinese: first to 500+; Japanese: call Stop with best hand.
timeline: 20th century and later: Chinese 51 is reported as a regional game around Nanping in northern Fujian, while Japanese 51 becomes a well-known family and children's game in Japan.

setup.players: 3-4 (standard). Optimal: 3-4. Chinese: 4 usual, 3 sometimes; Japanese: best 4.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack. Numeral cards 2-10 face value; Jack, Queen, King 10 each; Ace 11.
setup.dealing: Chinese: cards dealt one at a time anticlockwise; starter gets 6 cards, others 5. Japanese: dealer gives each player 5 cards, then 5 cards face up on table; rest form stock.

rules.objective: Chinese 51: Be first to 500+ points by making hands of five cards in one suit (A=11, K/Q/J=10, numeric=face). Japanese 51: Have the highest-scoring hand; sum best suit then subtract other suits; call "Stop!" when satisfied.
rules.gameplay: Chinese: draw and discard, exchange cards; make hands of five in one suit (51 max). Japanese: pick from board, discard; call Stop when satisfied; best single-suit total wins (other suits subtract).
keyRules: Same suit scores: A=11, K/Q/J=10, numeric=face value
Chinese: draw, discard, exchange; first to 500+
Japanese: pick board cards, call Stop; highest single-suit total wins

strategy.basic: Collect one suit; avoid mixing suits in Chinese 51. In Japanese 51, call Stop before opponents improve.
strategy.intermediate: Track discards; time your call in Japanese 51.
strategy.advanced: Block opponents' suits; go for 51-point hand (A-K-Q-J-10) when possible.
tips: Face cards 10 each, A 11; only same-suit hands score.

variations.name: Chinese 51 with Jokers
variations.description: Two jokers as wild cards, value 10; hand without joker beats equal hand with joker. Some play only call if hand scores at least 42.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This Chinese 51 variant only adjusts joker use and minimum call score; engine overrides for these parameters are not modeled yet.

variations.name: Bomb (Chinese)
variations.description: Four cards of same rank plus any fifth card counts as bomb; declare for 204 points.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: The bomb variant adds a 204-point four-of-a-kind bomb scoring rule that is not yet wired into engine overrides.

variations.name: Japanese 51 with Joker
variations.description: One joker as any card not in hand; worth 11 or 10 depending on ace. Some play that after Stop the table cannot be cleared.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: The Japanese joker variant changes card values and Stop clearing rules; those mechanical differences are not yet encoded as engine overrides.

scoring.description: In Chinese 51, only hands of five cards in one suit score, using A=11, K/Q/J=10 and numeral cards 2-10 at face value; declaring a perfect 51-point hand scores double and play continues until a player reaches or exceeds the agreed target (often 500 points). In Japanese 51, a five-card hand is valued by adding the points in the strongest suit and subtracting the points in the other suits, so totals can be positive or negative, and the highest final total after a Stop call wins the deal.
